title: perf-benchmarking-sync-2026-03-17
content:
Perf Benchmarking Sync - 2026-03-17

Attendees: Asha Patel (owner), Jonas Müller, Priya Singh, Miguel Torres, Daniel Kim, Li Wei (notes)

Summary
- Quick sync to triage the latency and throughput anomalies surfaced on 2026-03-16 nightly runs. Focus areas: 2048-token P50/P95 regressions for quantized llama-7b-v2, and decreased tokens/sec for heavy batching on GPU pool staging-rack-3.

Test matrix & environment
- Harness: bench-runner v0.12.1 (docker image: bench-runner:2026-03-15)
- Models: llama-7b-v2-quant (int8), llama-7b-v2-fp16, redwood-instruct-3b-qat
- Hardware: staging-rack-3 (4 x A100 80GB), staging-rack-1 (2 x A100 40GB) for comparison
- Serving runtime: commit a1b2c3d4 (main) - note: kernel selection logic changes merged 2026-03-15
- Test scenarios: short-chat (max_tokens 128), long-gen-2048 (max_tokens 2048), batch-heavy (batch=32, seq=1024)
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization, memory headroom, kv-cache hit rate

Findings (high level)
1) 2048-token latency regression (llama-7b-v2-quant):
   - Baseline (2026-03-10): p50=740ms, p95=2,100ms
   - Nightly (2026-03-16): p50=820ms (+10.8%), p95=2,350ms (+11.9%)
   - Observed increased host->device memcpy times and slightly higher CUDA kernel launch latency on staging-rack-3.
   - Regression surfaced after kernel-selection refactor (commit a1b2c3d4).

2) Throughput drop on batch-heavy runs:
   - Batch=32, seq=1024, llama-7b-v2-fp16
   - Tokens/sec baseline ~ 42k tps, current ~ 36k tps (-14%).
   - GPU occupancy lower than expected (~68% vs 82% baseline), more time spent on small kernels (attention split).
   - KV-cache effective hit-rate unchanged; suggests scheduling/launches rather than memory pressure.

3) Intermittent tail spikes (p99) across models:
   - p99 increased by ~18% in long-gen-2048 runs. Spikes correlate with sporadic rescheduling of worker threads on the host.
   - Linux perf traces show occasional context-switch bursts coinciding with kube-proxy flapping on the node.

Investigation notes
- Reproduced regression locally on staging-rack-3 using same harness and seed; reproduced p50/p95 increases consistently.
- Reverted kernel-selection logic to previous heuristic in a local build -> latency returned to baseline within noise (p50 change <2%). This points to the refactor as likely root cause.
- Micro-benchmarks: kernel launch times for fused-attn kernel increased by ~7-12% in new path, especially at longer sequence lengths.
- CUDA driver versions on staging-rack-3: 525.60.13; compare with staging-rack-1 (525.85.05). Driver difference may amplify latency sensitivity.
- Observed increased small memcpy operations in new code path; possible subtle change in buffer layout leading to more host staging copies.

Action items (owners & ETA)
- Asha: Create minimal repro and PR with toggle flag to opt into new kernel-selection at runtime; target PR by 2026-03-19. (blocked: need CI micro-bench capacity)
- Jonas: Run targeted kernel micro-bench suite across all staging racks and record launch times + memcpy times; due 2026-03-18. (in progress)
- Priya: Coordinate with infra to pin CUDA driver to 525.85.05 on one staging-rack-3 node for comparison; due 2026-03-18. (todo)
- Miguel: Add more detailed tracing around buffer allocation and memcpy calls in the refactor branch; instrument and push to perf bucket; due 2026-03-20. (todo)
- Daniel: Triage kube-proxy flapping on nodes that showed p99 spikes; open infra ticket if necessary (INFRA-2026); due 2026-03-18. (in progress)

Mitigation plan
- Short-term: enable runtime opt-out for new kernel selection so Dedicated/Hosted traffic can be routed to stable path while investigating. Rollout gating: default=stable, opt-in=new for canaries.
- Medium-term: if kernel-selection refactor is confirmed root cause, rework selection heuristics to preserve previous launch patterns for long sequences; include a flagset for memcpy/buffer layout behavior.

Notes / Questions
- Is there any customer traffic pattern that would uniquely surface this regression? (Priya) -> Likely customers with high long-context runs (>=1024) and low-latency SLOs; surface in console as potential risk.
- Should we add a dedicated nightly for long-gen 2048 across all racks to catch regressions earlier? Consensus: yes, Jonas to add to bench-runner schedule and alert thresholds.

Follow-ups
- Next sync: 2026-03-19 (standup format) to review Jonas micro-bench results and Asha repro PR status.
- If PR toggle validated, plan canary rollout starting 2026-03-20 on 5% traffic.

Attachments / Links
- Bench logs: s3://redwood-perf/benchlogs/2026-03-16/longgen-2048/
- Repro branch: git://repo/branches/bugfix/kernel-selection-repro-a1b2
- Infra ticket for driver parity (opened by Priya) -> INFRA-DRIVER-74

Raw snippets (copied from runs)
- baseline p50/p95 (llama-7b-v2-quant long-gen): 740ms / 2100ms
- nightly p50/p95: 820ms / 2350ms
- batch-heavy tokens/sec: baseline 42000, current 36000
- kernel launch times (fused-attn): baseline avg 0.82ms -> new path avg 0.92ms at seq=1024

Unresolved
- Exact interaction between CUDA driver diff and new code path still unknown.
- Need reproducible micro-benchmark that isolates memcpy behavior across buffer layouts.

Notes to self
- Keep short-gen nightly unchanged while investigating; minimize risk to low-latency users.
- Add a dashboard card in Console for daily long-gen p95 trend and an automated alert if p95 increases >8% vs 7-day median.
